[Performance][MRV1] Commit only dirty block-table ranges (#17066)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR optimizes the legacy Model Runner V1 block-table commit path. It
does not modify Model Runner V2.

MRv1 currently copies every active block-table row at its full logical
width on each commit. For long-context decode, the actual change is
usually only a small appended suffix. This PR:

- tracks the changed interval of each MRv1 request row
- packs the dirty block IDs and compact metadata into double-buffered
staging buffers
- scatters the packed payload into the persistent device block table
with a Triton kernel
- preserves the device table address, shape, and stride used by slot
mapping and attention
- splits long dirty ranges into 1024-entry scatter segments

MRv2 already uses upstream `StagedWriteTensor` / `FusedStagedWriter`
incremental updates, so no MRv2 implementation change is required.

An earlier DSV4 DP16 decode profile of this MRv1 design reduced
block-table H2D time from approximately 2.72 ms/step to 0.14 ms/step.
The profile predates this current-main adaptation and is motivation
rather than current-main benchmark evidence.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The optimized MRv1 path is enabled by default. It can be disabled only
through platform additional configuration:

```bash
--additional-config '{"block_table_no_commit_optimize": 1}'\n```\n\n- omitted or `0`: use dirty-range commits\n- `1`: restore the original full-copy MRv1 path\n\nThe legacy `VLLM_ASCEND_BLOCK_TABLE_NO_COMMIT_OPTIMIZE` environment variable is not supported. The option is typed as `Literal[0, 1]`; other values fail configuration validation.\n\nThis option affects MRv1 only. MRv2 already has incremental block-table updates and ignores it. The compatibility option will be removed together with MRv1 when MRv1 is retired.\n\n### How was this patch tested?\n\n- Added MRv1 unit coverage for append, move, swap, dirty-range reset, CPU commit equivalence, and additional-config path selection.\n- Verified the final diff contains no MRv2 block-table changes.\n- Added the option, scope, legacy environment-variable status, MRv2 behavior, and MRv1 retirement policy to the additional-configuration documentation.\n- Repository pre-commit checks passed: Ruff check/format, codespell, typos, gitleaks, import and policy checks, and DCO sign-off.\n- `python3 -m compileall` and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.\n\nNPU execution was not run locally. Required follow-up coverage on Ascend is MRv1 single/multi-rank model smoke, prefix-cache and KV-cache mutation cases, plus the Triton scatter dtype/shape/layout matrix.

[Feature][KV Pool] Support Mamba in Mooncake layerwise (#17287)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake hybrid layerwise currently rejects layouts containing recurrent
Mamba state. Removing that check alone is unsafe: GDN, Kimi KDA, and
other Mamba-like layers update conv/recurrent state inside attention, so
an attention-entry PUT can publish the previous state while the
following request reports a cache hit.

This change:

- identifies physical layers containing `MambaSpec`, including per-layer
`UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`;
- keeps full/sliding-window attention PUTs at attention entry;
- preserves the post-compute save hook for recurrent layers so Mooncake
publishes updated state;
- reuses the stage-local layer mapping and PP-scoped key namespace from
#17183, mapping global recurrent layer names to the correct local layer
on each pipeline stage;
- applies the existing send-backlog policy to recurrent and record-only
save paths;
- drains queued PUTs at step completion, including when the final layer
has no ranges to save.

The generic GDN/Mamba load, deferred state-copy, and connector hooks
from #12711 are already present on main. This PR only adds the Mooncake
block-key publication semantics. The implementation and lifecycle
coverage are based on #17194 and credit its author in the commit.

[Refactor][Feature][DCP] Unify speculative decoding metadata for MLA (#17336)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Align Ascend MLA DCP metadata with upstream vLLM's `dcp_local_seq_lens`
flow across model runners V1/V2 and MTP/DSpark speculative decoding. The
previous paths relied on separate legacy metadata and did not
consistently propagate draft sequence lengths to the MLA backend.

producers. MLA consumes the CPU lengths required by FIA; SFA shares the

indexing and upstream `cp_local_slot`, so KV writes respect rank
ownership and interleave size.

No. This fixes MLA DCP speculative-decoding metadata and KV slot mapping

[Feature][MRV2] Extend fine-grained TP support (MLP, embedding) to model runner v2 (#17361)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Extends fine-grained TP on model runner v2 beyond o_proj, on top of the
framework landed in #16967 (and its prerequisite #17128). The four knobs
split into two families with different contracts:

1. **MLP TP joins the o_proj (uniform-token) contract.** The MLP
exchange (gate_up `all_gather` / down `reduce_scatter` over DP-axis
groups) needs the same group-uniform token count per step as o_proj, so
`mlp_tensor_parallel_size > 1` joins the graph-mode / PCP / `tp == 1` /
PD-scenario checks, the capture-bound auto-disable (a miss disables both
knobs together — the bound is a property of the step, not of a knob),
the `PreemptOffloadConnector` gate, the offload-failure abort, and the
eager-step guard (renamed `_check_finegrained_tp_graph_step`).
2. **Embedding TP is capacity-based and joins none of the uniform-token
checks.** Its exchange pads every step to a fixed capacity inside the
op, so it is step-shape-agnostic and cannot desync; the runtime capacity
already floors at `max_num_batched_tokens`, so its one real failure mode
fails fast on its own.
3. **The recompute-scheduler requirement covers all four knobs.** o_proj
and embedding already required it on main; mlp joins as it enters the
uniform-token contract, and lmhead joins so the whole
`finegrained_tp_config` stays within the one configuration validated
end-to-end. The first traffic test of the no-recompute path on the PD
test bed produced deterministically wrong outputs with every knob off (a
pre-existing defect unrelated to this PR, tracked separately), so that
path stays outside the supported set until it is fixed.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- `mlp_tensor_parallel_size` now works on the V2 runner in graph-mode
PD-decode deployments, with the same preconditions as
`oproj_tensor_parallel_size`.
- All four `finegrained_tp_config` sizes require
`recompute_scheduler_enable=true` (previously only o_proj and embedding
did).
- At runtime, an eagerly dispatched step under o_proj/MLP TP fails the
request with an explicit error (the message now names both knobs).

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests**: one new case in `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` (MLP
capture-bound, incl. the both-knobs-disabled-together semantics); the
remaining gates are shared conditions already covered by the existing
o_proj cases. CI on the current head: `pre-commit` and `cpu-ut` green.

**End-to-end** — single-node A3 (16 chips), PD disaggregation behind the
LB proxy; DeepSeek-V3.1-arch W8A8 checkpoint truncated to 6 layers (real
weights, `--quantization ascend`). P = chip 0 (`tp1`, eager, Mooncake
producer); D = chips 8-15 (`dp8 × tp1`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture size
512, recompute scheduler on, `MultiConnector` = Mooncake consumer +
`PreemptOffloadConnector`); every request goes through the proxy. Each
round: 8-concurrent × 256-token bench × 3 (6144 tokens) plus 5 fixed
greedy prompts for consistency.

Positive rounds (all: 8/8 startup, 100% of bench tokens, knob reported
enabled, zero guard hits, zero auto-disables, zero collective errors):

| Round | Engine TPOT | Output vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 7.12 ms | — |
| `mlp=2` | 7.33 ms | 1/5 prompts identical, the rest diverge at the
first token (see note) |
| `oproj=2 + mlp=2` | 7.24 ms | same class as `mlp=2`; bit-identical to
the three-knob round |
| `embedding=2` | 7.32 ms | **5/5 bit-identical** |
| all three knobs | 7.14 ms | bit-identical to the `oproj=2+mlp=2` round
|

Consistency note: re-sharding o_proj/MLP changes the reduction order,
and the truncated 6-layer test model has a near-flat output
distribution, so the greedy pick can flip at the first token — the same
class of difference as changing the generic TP size. The embedding
exchange is pure data movement and stays bit-identical, including when
stacked with the other two knobs.

Negative configs (rejected or disabled at startup, no hang):

| Config | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `mlp=2` + `--enforce-eager` | rejected at config load ("only supported
in graph mode") |
| `mlp=2` without `PreemptOffloadConnector` | rejected with the explicit
connector requirement |
| `mlp=2` without the recompute scheduler | rejected at config load in
~15 s with the recompute-scheduler requirement (the all-knobs gate
above) |
| capture bound 512 < largest step 600 | both knobs auto-disabled with a
warning; startup completes |

Base controls: the rounds above ran on the base before #17159; since
#17159 reworked the embedding exchange, the embedding-relevant cells
were re-run on the current base — baseline and `embedding=2` outputs are
**bit-identical** to the pre-#17159 results (TPOT 7.52 / 7.18 ms). A
no-recompute control on the current base produced deterministically
wrong outputs with **every knob off** (a pre-existing defect, tracked
separately); `embedding=2` on that path is bit-identical to the no-knob
run, i.e. fine-grained TP adds no effect — this is the defect behind the
all-knobs recompute requirement.

**Memory** (same bed): the family's fixed cost is one HCCL buffer set
(~0.42 GB per rank, from #16967); MLP saves 0.55 GiB per rank at `mlp=2`
on the 6-layer bed (dense-FFN layers × 1/2), o_proj 0.109 GiB per layer
per rank on a 1-byte checkpoint (#16967).

[Bugfix][Spec Decode]  Update MRV2 eager draft attention metadata before decode (#17206)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Ascend V2 autoregressive speculator rebuilds draft attention
metadata for every draft step in eager mode. Previously, the
Ascend-specific CPU-side sequence lengths were updated only after the
draft forward. That update was too late for the current FIA call and was
then discarded when the next draft step rebuilt its metadata. As a
result, later Eagle3 draft positions used stale sequence-length metadata
and had lower acceptance rates.

This PR updates the freshly built attention metadata inside
`_build_draft_attn_metadata`, before it is consumed by the upcoming
draft decode. It also adds a regression test that verifies the current
draft step and request count are applied before the builder returns.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It improves speculative-decoding acceptance and throughput for the
V2 model runner when using Ascend eager autoregressive draft decoding.
There is no API or configuration change.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit test:

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q tests/ut/spec_decode/test_autoregressive_draft_metadata.py
```

Result: `2 passed`. `python -m py_compile` and `git diff --check` also
passed for the changed files.

End-to-end benchmark used Qwen3-32B with its Eagle3 speculator,
`num_speculative_tokens=3`, V2 model runner, `--enforce-eager`, full
GSM8K (1,319 samples), and concurrency 64. All sampling and server
settings were kept identical.

| Run | Accuracy | Overall acceptance | Position 1 / 2 / 3 | API
inference time | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V1 baseline | 95.8302% | 66.6667% | 82.9463% / 66.7158% / 50.3380% |
176.62 s | 1703.4 token/s |
| V2 before | 95.5269% | 65.5024% | 83.0093% / 65.7108% / 47.7872% |
144.62 s | 2082.0 token/s |
| V2 after | 95.5269% | 66.6017% | 82.8641% / 66.7343% / 50.2068% |
137.61 s | 2187.5 token/s |

The V2 acceptance rate improved by 1.0993 percentage points and is now
within 0.0650 percentage points of V1. The largest recovery is at the

[BugFix] Add off-stride graph capture size ceilings (#16970)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix off-stride default CUDAGraph capture sizes on Ascend. Fixes #16049 .

When `max_num_seqs` is not on the default capture-size grid, the largest
decode batches could fall back to eager execution. This change preserves
Ascend's reduced capture ceiling for memory savings while adding the
exact ceiling to the capture-size list before upstream finalizes the
graph configuration.

For example, `max_num_seqs=77` now produces a capture size of 77 and
dispatches the largest decode batch to a FULL graph.

## Why this approach?

The exact ceiling is added while reusing upstream capture-size
generation and filtering, so Ascend does not duplicate the upstream
size-grid logic. Rounding the ceiling to 8/16, as in PR #16692, leaves
the padded graph unreachable for FULL decode; duplicating the grid
logic, as in PR #16623, increases long-term maintenance cost.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new configuration option is introduced. Off-stride default decode
batches can now use CUDAGraphs instead of falling back to eager
execution.

## How was this patch tested?

- `tests/ut/test_platform.py`
- A/B configuration and dispatcher check with `max_num_seqs=77`
- Baseline: capture sizes ended at 72 and batch 77 dispatched to `NONE`
- Fixed: capture sizes include 77 and batch 77 dispatched to `FULL`
- Result: `93 passed, 1 skipped`

commits.message:
[BugFix][Spec Decode] Correct rejected token seq_lens in MRV1 (#14883)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

ModelRunner V1 does not subtract rejected target tokens from the
device-side `seq_lens` before building the later one-token draft decode
steps. SFA and DSA consume this tensor as the exact KV sequence length.
Consequently, their later draft Attention steps use an overestimated
sequence length that still includes rejected token positions.

The issue was observed by printing the rejected-token count and the
device-side sequence lengths used by three consecutive draft steps:

```text
[V1_DEVICE_SEQ_LENS] rejected=[3] steps=[[47], [48], [49]]
[V1_DEVICE_SEQ_LENS] rejected=[2] steps=[[56], [57], [58]]
[V1_DEVICE_SEQ_LENS] rejected=[3] steps=[[98], [99], [100]]
```

The sequence lengths advance by one for each draft step, but their
baseline is not reduced by the corresponding rejected-token count.
Therefore, the device-side `seq_lens` is overestimated by 3, 2, and 3
tokens in these examples. SFA-style model backends pass this incorrect
value to both the sparse Indexer and the Attention kernel as the exact
KV sequence length. As a result, both the Indexer and Attention execute
with an overestimated KV length that includes the rejected token
positions.

This PR preserves the unadjusted sequence lengths used by merged step 0,
then copies them to an independent NPU buffer and subtracts rejected
tokens for the remaining one-token draft decode steps. The CPU-side
sequence lengths remain an optimistic upper bound to avoid an NPU-to-CPU
synchronization.

[BugFix][Model] Make MiniMax-M3 prefill KV-gather-Q optional on A5 (#17241)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow up on #14685: A3 already falls back when the experimental
Split-KV package is absent, but A5 currently skips the availability
check and unconditionally calls the vendor prefill entry point.

- Select the prefill path by optional Split-KV ACLNN availability before
building K2Q, without a separate device allowlist. Remove the unused
`MINIMAX_M3_PREFILL_KV_GATHER_Q` capability declaration and
registrations; retain `FP8_ATTENTION` for dtype validation and existing
precision-mode selection.
- Use the existing Q-gather-KV prefill path when the package is
unavailable.
- Extend that fallback to A5 E4M3 KV caches: cast/clamp Q consistently
with decode, supply unit dequantization scales, and return BF16 output.
Variable per-request query lengths and the original `-1` top-k sentinels
are preserved.
- Harden the native availability probe: require both entry points from
the same provider and reject the **known metadata-enabled experimental
ABI**, which adds `metadataOptional` to the workspace-size signature
without renaming the entry point. Inspect the selected provider so a
lower-priority incompatible library does not disable a compatible
provider.

This does not add support for the metadata-enabled ABI or attempt
universal ABI detection. It safely falls back for that known
incompatible package. Compatible packages retain the current KV-gather-Q
path. Precision modes and decode are unchanged. The dedicated
KV-gather-Q hardware capability is removed; other capability
definitions, including `FP8_ATTENTION`, are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MiniMax-M3 A5 prefill no longer requires the optional experimental
Split-KV package: it can use Q-gather-KV with BF16 or E4M3 KV caches.

Dispatch now depends solely on the ACLNN availability probe, not the
former A3/A5 capability allowlist. A device previously excluded by that
allowlist will also attempt KV-gather-Q if the probe succeeds. Users
must install a package containing kernels for the actual SoC: the probe
does not verify device-kernel compatibility, and execution errors are
not automatically caught and retried on the fallback path. The mocked A2
dispatch test verifies routing only, not A2 hardware support.

To enable KV-gather-Q, install a **compatible** experimental package,
source its environment, and restart the workers. No source-code change
or new environment switch is needed. The availability result and loader
search paths are cached per process; installing a package into an
already running worker is not supported.

commits.message:
[Performance] Optimize rotary embedding application in DeepSeek V4 by running in-place (#16978)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
`DSparkModel._project_shared_kv` now applies RoPE in place on the
rope-segment view of the normalized kv tensor, instead of materializing
the rope segment and re-assembling `[k_nope | k_pe]` with `split -> rope
-> cat -> contiguous` . The previous implementation paid for a full
extra read+write of the `[num_tokens, head_dim]` kv tensor on every
call: the rope segment was detached via `split` , rotated into a fresh
tensor, and then `torch.cat` reassembled a buffer that is numerically
identical to `kv` itself (only the rope segment changes; the nope
segment is passed through untouched).
`ComplexExpRotaryEmbedding.forward` ends with `y.copy_(...)` , i.e.
`npu_rotary_mul` writes its result back to the input storage. Running
the rope directly on a view of `kv` therefore produces the same final
values while the nope segment never moves and no concat buffer is
allocated.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
NO.

[BugFix][SFA] Align DP-padded inputs with attention metadata (#16768)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #16799.

With uneven DP batches, draft model execution is synchronized to the
maximum token count across DP ranks, while draft attention metadata
describes only the real queries on the current rank. In SFA speculative
decoding this can produce DP-padded `hidden_states` with shorter `cos`,
`sin`, and slot mappings. Passing those tensors directly to
`npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache` causes a leading-dimension mismatch.

This is a regression exposed by an upstream vLLM behavior change:

- vllm-project/vllm#54856 introduced `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync`,
allowing autoregressive draft execution to reuse the target batch's
DP-synchronized token count.
- vllm-project/vllm#55458 then changed draft attention metadata to
exclude DP-only model padding by using `batch_desc.num_reqs` instead of
`batch_desc.num_tokens` for `num_tokens_padded`.

PR #55458 directly introduced the shape split seen by Ascend SFA: the
draft model can still execute `batch_desc.num_tokens`, while its
attention metadata now contains only `batch_desc.num_reqs` rows on the
lower-load DP rank. This patch adapts vllm-ascend to that upstream
contract without changing upstream vLLM.

The fix:

- trims DP-only model padding only when graph dispatch has fallen back
to eager (`CUDAGraphMode.NONE`);
- trims before Prolog V3 and MLAPO preprocessing, and after the native
parallel-layout input transformation so CP-local layouts remain intact;
- keeps native KV, gate, and indexer inputs aligned with the real query
count;
- zero-pads the attention result back to the preallocated model output
shape.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration change. It fixes SFA speculative decoding with
uneven DP batches.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`
- 8-NPU GLM-5.2 W4A8 validation: TP=4, DP=2, MTP=3, 100 GSM8K prompts,
concurrency=8, max output length=8192. All 100 requests completed with
zero request failures and 98% accuracy. Runtime logs covered uneven DP
loads including 3/5 and 2/1 without shape errors or hangs.

[BugFix][Engram] Skip HOST_UVA page migration during CPU binding (#17348)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17286.

With Engram HOST_UVA offload, post-warmup CPU binding runs
`migratepages` after the large host tables have already been registered
and pinned. Migrating the whole worker can stall startup for many
minutes, and DP replicas sharing a backing can request different NUMA
destinations.

Keep CPU thread and IRQ affinity at the existing
post-warmup/post-capture point, but skip process-wide page migration
when `engram_config.cpu_offload` is enabled. Move the migration call out
of the thread-binding methods so it can be skipped independently. Other
configurations retain the existing migration behavior and ordering.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Engram HOST_UVA workloads can keep CPU binding enabled without the
process-wide `migratepages` startup stall. No new configuration is
required. Shared-table placement and selective page migration are
outside this fix.

### How was this patch tested?

- The complete existing CPU-binding and V1 worker unit-test files passed
(151 tests). Only existing CPU-binding expectations were updated for the
migration call location and argument forwarding. No new test cases were
added; mock-only tests cannot reproduce the pinned HOST_UVA
page-migration stall, which was validated on hardware as described
below.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Standalone validation, Ascend `2cd0042f1`: A3, CANN 9.1, 16 NPUs,
TP2/DP8, shared Engram HOST_UVA, async scheduling, DSpark5 with eager
draft, and FULL_DECODE_ONLY. All 16 workers completed post-capture
affinity binding in 4-7 seconds; 1,257 measured requests succeeded. Two
fixed 128-token probes matched the no-binding control exactly in tokens
and logprobs. This ran under UID 1000, so IRQ writes were skipped due to
permissions.
- Full P/D (1P1D) rerun on this PR head, external DP, Engram HOST_UVA
with `{"cpu_offload": true, "dp_shared_memory": true}` and
`enable_cpu_binding: true`, single-node TP4/DP4 prefill plus TP2/DP8
decode on 16 NPUs each, V1 runner, DSpark5, decode side on async
scheduling with FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Every worker logged `CPU affinity
applied without process-wide NUMA page migration.` and no `migratepages`
process appeared on either node. Both halves reached ready: prefill in
353.5 s, decode in 475-513 s. Twelve measured `vllm bench serve` runs
(128/4096 input, 256 output, concurrency 1/8/32, temperature 0)
completed with mean ITL 37.4-50.2 ms and 66-643 output tok/s.
- Control on the PR merge base without this patch, same deployment: the
decode half never reached ready. Up to 16 `migratepages` helpers
appeared right after graph capture, EngineCore repeatedly reported `No
available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds`, and the
helpers were still running more than 45 minutes later, with their target
worker stuck in state `D` and `kill -9` having no effect.

[Feature][AscendStore] Prepare V4.1 and speculative cache reuse (#16973)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Prepare non-layerwise Ascend Store for DeepSeek V4.1's mixed C1/C2,
sliding-window and private circular-state layout. Private state
currently participates in hash-size selection, hit lookup and transfer:
it can choose a 32-token hash unit instead of 128, reject an explicit
128-token unit, or persist a request-private ring under prefix keys.

Use the existing `prefix_cacheable` capability to exclude private groups
from hashing/alignment, external hit coordination and key generation,
preserving original group IDs and locally allocated state. After
reserving the final token, private-state layouts resume at a token-page
boundary: a fully cached 512-token prompt loads 384 tokens; a 513-token
prompt can load 512. Existing non-speculative layouts without private
state retain their 511-token hit for a 512-token prompt.

Also fix a pre-existing non-layerwise speculative decode-save issue,
reproduced on unmodified main with both MTP and DSpark. With
`save_decode_cache=true`, lookahead can cross a page before committed
request hashes exist; advancing the saved cursor then loses the eventual
valid page. Reusing already allocated lookahead blocks can also skip the
save step. Follow the scheduler's post-rejection token count, cap
full-page save progress at available hashes, and process decode saves
even without new block allocation.

This PR changes **Ascend Store only**. Main now includes the V4.1
framework restored in #16925; no framework code is added by this PR.
Engram weight placement/TP sharding is unchanged. Engram prompt-history
restoration and GLM5.3/private-tail support are outside this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Non-layerwise hybrid layouts with private state can reuse external KV at
valid page boundaries. MTP/DSpark decode pages completed after
speculative rejection remain reusable when decode saving is enabled. No
new option, dependency or key format. Layerwise transfer with private
state remains explicitly rejected.

[BugFix][WeightTransfer] Destroy native HCCL communicators on shutdown (#17154)

HCCL weight transfer previously dropped its Python communicator
reference on shutdown without destroying the native communicator.
Reinitialization also replaced the previous communicator without closing
it.

Add an idempotent `close()` that synchronizes the communicator's device
before calling `hcclCommDestroy`. Call it during shutdown and before
reinitialization. Reuse the existing availability flag to prevent
repeated destruction and reject collectives on a closed communicator.
Initialization, warmup, weight reception, and exception propagation
remain unchanged; no restart policy or new exception type is introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Shutdown and reinitialization explicitly release the native HCCL
communicator. Calling a collective on an already closed communicator
raises `RuntimeError`.

directories using the repository's CPU/mock UT setup and CI-pinned vLLM
revision `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c` (Python 3.11,
PyTorch 2.10.0).
- Regression coverage verifies device synchronization before
destruction, repeated/disabled close, close failures, rejection of
collectives after close, and engine shutdown/reinitialization.

(`--follow-imports skip --check-untyped-defs`, Python 3.11 target),
syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

```

[Performance][Attention] Reuse device cache-store dispatch for SFA C8 (#17135)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Route both native and DSA-CP main SFA C8 cache writes through
`DeviceOperator.try_scatter_cache`, following MiniMax's
actual-token-prefix calling pattern. The device adaptor selects the
existing SK path on A2/A3 and PA path on A5. It also executes
`torch_npu.npu_scatter_nd_update_` itself when the fast path is
unavailable or does not support the input, so the SFA caller has one
call and no separate fallback branch.

The public method performs cache writes in place and returns `None`.
`_scatter_cache` is called in a separate statement, and its internal
result controls whether generic fallback is needed. Both paths preserve
the original destination storage and actual-token slicing. Native
preprocessing keeps the packed NoPE/RoPE/scale byte order and supplies
its own SFA slot mapping; padding beyond num_actual_tokens is excluded.
Operator exceptions propagate without retrying a possibly partial write.
Layouts the original generic operator cannot handle remain unsupported;
no contiguous destination copy is introduced.

Remove `prefill_cache_write_enabled`, its 2048-token threshold, the
`fast_cache_store` metadata field/gate, and capture-builder overrides
that only disabled that gate. Dispatch no longer depends on prefill
state or node role. Native operator implementations, MiniMax callers, LI
C8, and compressed-cache callers are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

SFA C8 batches attempt the existing device-specific cache store
regardless of prefill/decode state or batch size. There is no new
configuration setting.

**Known unresolved boundary:** actual-token slicing excludes tail
padding but does not filter negative slots inside the active prefix. No
negative-slot or native-kernel fix is included. An earlier instrumented
model run observed eight active `-1` slots during non-capture
speculative prewarm and stopped before invoking SK. Safety for that case
or model graph metadata containing active negative slots is not
established by this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

Current commit: `1279724cf2d5a8a7a7d8294324b6411b49a44bf8`.

- **311 unit tests passed** with CPU-only mocks
(`TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0`):
`tests/ut/attention/test_cache_store.py`,
`tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`,
`tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_cp.py`,
`tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py`, and
`tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py`. Coverage checks the `None` return
contract for fast and generic paths, platform dispatch, exactly one
generic fallback, actual-token slicing, destination storage, shape
guards, and exception propagation without a second write.
- Ruff lint, Ruff format, and `git diff --check` passed. `bash format.sh
ci` was attempted but could not run because local `pre-commit` is not
installed.
- **28/28 A3 NPU tests passed** on Ascend910_9362 with unchanged native
binaries: 24 fast-path cases compare the complete backing storage across
dtypes, widths, row strides, offsets, and token counts; one case checks
supported generic float32 fallback including negative slots; one
compares unsupported inner-stride behavior with the original generic
operator; two exercise native SFA C8 packing and actual-token writes
with 3/2049 tokens and negative padding outside the active prefix. The
runtime verified 4142 source files and 1281 native manifest entries.
Test source hashes match the committed production code. The test
container exited 0 and its NPU processes/device locks were released.
- A2/A5 hardware and full-model throughput have not been validated for
this head. Four-machine attempt `opt3-20260922T084208Z` stopped during
instrumented model prewarm before any benchmark request: all 64 workers
passed the SFA/LI C8 runtime audit, but all 32 decode workers reached
the native main-KV store with 128 active negative slots (`int8
[128,656]`, not capturing). The validation guard stopped execution
before invoking SK. This is not an observed native-kernel crash or a
measured throughput regression. No benchmark client was created and no
throughput value was obtained, so the unchanged 1265.6172 × 0.97 =
1227.648684 output tokens/s target remains unverified. All four
task-owned containers exited and their NPU processes/locks were
released; automatic retries are paused pending resolution of the warmup
boundary. Negative-slot success on the generic fallback does not
establish negative-slot support in SK or PA.

Earlier cache-write microbenchmark results were collected for the call

`1279724cf2d5a8a7a7d8294324b6411b49a44bf8` maps SFA C8 `-1` slots to

[Feature][MRV2] Support o_proj TP in model runner v2 (graph-mode scope) (#16967)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enables `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` (fine-grained TP for the attention
output projection) on model runner v2, scoped to its real deployment: a
PD decode node (`tp == 1`, `dp > 1`, MoE) running a graph mode with the
recompute scheduler.

The o_proj exchange (`all_to_all` → partial GEMM → `reduce_scatter`) is
an `all_to_all_single` without split sizes: every rank must forward the
same number of tokens per step, or the collectives hang silently. In
graph mode the upstream dispatch already guarantees that group-uniform
count, so this PR adds no runner-side padding — it adds the contract
that keeps the count uniform, and guardrails that turn a silent hang
into an explicit failure:

1. Graph mode is required: `cudagraph_mode == NONE` (which covers
`enforce_eager`) is rejected at config load.
2. Capture-bound check: the knob is kept only if the largest capture
size covers the largest possible step (`min(max_num_batched_tokens,
max_num_seqs * decode_query_len)`); otherwise it is disabled with a
warning and the deployment still starts.
3. A guard at the top of `NPUModelRunner.prepare_inputs` — the only
post-dispatch hook, reached by real steps only — raises an explicit
`RuntimeError` if a step still dispatches to eager. Armed only for a
real split (`> 1`).
4. PCP (`prefill_context_parallel_size > 1`) is rejected: its per-rank
token recount breaks the uniform step size.
5. With `> 1`, the KV connector chain must carry
`PreemptOffloadConnector` — startup fails without it — and an offload
failure at preemption aborts the request instead of sending it back to
P. Checked in `platform._check_ascend_config` because MultiConnector
children re-derive the config from per-child copies that cannot see
their siblings.

Existing preconditions unchanged: PD decode node (`is_kv_consumer`),
`recompute_scheduler_enable=true`, `tensor_parallel_size == 1`, MoE.

Depends on #17128 (reclassifies the request-arrival boundary recompute
as decode, so those steps stay on captured graphs); this PR is meant to
land after it.

### Design conclusions (aligned with the SE)

The scope and guardrails of this PR implement conclusions aligned with
the SE:

1. **No MRV1 parity goal.** Fine-grained TP is adapted to model runner
v2 only where necessary and reasonable; the bar is expected functional
correctness, not parity with MRV1.
2. **Preconditions are enforced at config load.**
`oproj_tensor_parallel_size` requires the recompute scheduler, preempt
offload, a graph mode, and a pure-DP PD decode deployment (`tp == 1`,
`dp > 1`).
3. **No eager fallback from an oversized step.** A step whose token
count exceeds the largest captured size dispatches to eager in every
graph mode; a conservative config-time check verifies the capture bound
covers the largest possible step and disables the knob otherwise. Other
fine-grained TP knobs can follow the same pattern.
4. **No return-to-P fallback under this feature.** Recompute preemption
is paired with offload; the stock path sends the request back to P when
the offload itself fails. This feature rejects that branch —
recomputation on P cannot guarantee computation equivalence — and fails
the request immediately with an explicit error instead.
5. **`PreemptOffloadConnector` is mandatory.** Config load rejects a
real split whose KV connector chain does not carry it.

### Memory cost and expected savings

The memory profile belongs to the feature, not to this PR — the
validation and guard paths allocate no device memory. Measured on the
test bed (DeepSeek-V3.1-arch W8A8 checkpoint truncated to 6 layers, `dp8
× tp1`, graph mode, identical connector config; per rank):

| Item | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed cost: HCCL buffers of the o_proj TP communication group | ~0.42
GB | measured (steady-state device delta; the freed weight is cancelled
by the larger KV pool); allocated at graph-capture time |
| Weight saving per layer, 1-byte (W8A8/FP8) checkpoint | 0.109 GiB × (1
− 1/N) | measured: 0.33 GiB @ `oproj=2`, 0.49 GiB @ `oproj=4` on 6
layers |
| Full 61-layer extrapolation, W8A8/FP8, `oproj=8` | ~5.8 GB gross, ~5.4
GB net of the fixed cost | from the measured per-layer slope |
| Net savings, DeepSeek-R1-W8A8, `oproj=8` | 5.8 GB | feature guide
(`Fine_grained_TP.md`) |
| DeepSeek-V3/R1 BF16, `oproj=8` | ~11.2 GiB net | from checkpoint dims
(0.219 GiB per layer) |

The freed weight memory returns to the KV cache, and the fixed cost is
recovered after ~8 layers at `oproj=2` (~4 at `oproj=8`) on a 1-byte
quantized checkpoint — trivially met by production-scale MoE models.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` now works on the V2 runner in graph-mode
PD-decode deployments; previously it was V1-only.
- New config-load rejections: `cudagraph_mode=none` / `enforce_eager`,
`prefill_context_parallel_size > 1`, and — for a real split — a KV
connector chain without `PreemptOffloadConnector`.
- Capture-bound auto-disable with a warning instead of rejection; raise
`max_cudagraph_capture_size` to use the knob at large `max_num_seqs`.
- An eagerly dispatched step now fails the request with an explicit
error instead of hanging; an offload failure at preemption aborts the
request instead of returning it to P.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests**: new cases in `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py`
(graph-mode / PCP rejection, size-1 exemption, capture-bound matrix),
`tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_finegrained_tp.py` (eager-step
guard contract) and `tests/ut/core/test_recompute_scheduler.py`
(offload-failure abort). CI on the current head: `pre-commit` (incl.
mypy) and `cpu-ut` green (5718 passed, 67 skipped).

**End-to-end** (single-node A3, 16 chips, PD disaggregation behind the
LB proxy, 8-layer MiniMax-M3 with dummy weights — functional/consistency
numbers, not real-weight performance): P = chip 0, `tp1` eager, Mooncake
producer; D = chips 8-15, `dp8 × tp1`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` + recompute
scheduler + `oproj_tensor_parallel_size=2`, Mooncake consumer; all
traffic through the proxy.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| config rejections | graph-mode and PD-scenario rejections fail startup
with explicit messages; `--max-num-seqs 600` (600 > 512) auto-disables
the knob with a warning and startup continues into graph capture |
| continuous PD traffic, `oproj=2` | 100% of requests completed, guard
fired 0 times, decode ran on captured FULL graphs, engine TPOT cc1/cc8
median 7.21 / 7.58 ms (990.7 tok/s at cc8) |
| vs `oproj=0` baseline | TPOT +0.07 ms (~1%); outputs token-identical
on 5 fixed prompts in every round |
| negative control (same topology without #17128) | the first arrival
step dispatches to eager → explicit `RuntimeError` within 3.7 s, no hang
|
| offload chain (`MultiConnector`: Mooncake + `PreemptOffloadConnector`)
| starts, graph capture OK, cc8 7.67 ms / 943 tok/s, outputs identical,
CPU offload pool active on 8/8 decode ranks |
| tight-KV sweeps (`gpu-memory-utilization` 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.35, 100 MB CPU
pool) | 100% of requests completed, outputs identical, no crash |

**Left uncovered** (for honesty): the preemption/offload runtime path
(KV save/restore and the capacity fallback) was not triggered —
preemption is unreachable on the 8-layer dummy model — so the
abort-instead-of-return-to-P branch is covered by unit tests only; and
the without-connector startup failure is a config-load check that has
not been reproduced e2e yet (it was observed on the test bed while the
check still warned).

[Test][Model] Replace the eight-card DSpark PP e2e with a four-card TP2xPP2 case (#17052)

## Summary

Replace
`tests/e2e/pull_request/eight_card/model_runner_v2/test_spec_pp_accuracy.py`
with a four-card variant at
`tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/model_runner_v2/test_spec_pp_accuracy.py`
running the same DeepSeek-V4 DSpark + PP accuracy check as **TP2 x
PP2**, full-layer (no `hf_overrides`).

The case keeps everything else from the merged eight-card test verbatim:
the `UploadWeight/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-w4a8-test` checkpoint, greedy
GSM8K decode with the `answer:71` golden, and `spec_decode_num_drafts` /
`num_accepted_tokens_per_pos` counter assertions.

## Why four cards, not two

The DSpark-w4a8-test checkpoint is ~168 GiB of quantized weights
(43-layer / 256-expert Flash, ~277B parameters), so it needs at least 4
x 64GB NPUs to host weights plus a KV cache. Two cards would require
`hf_overrides` layer trimming, which is not needed for accuracy coverage
and previously masked real signal with trimming-specific weight-loading
and cache-planning failures (trimmed layers miss weights in the DSpark
target loader, and shrinking `num_hidden_layers` without remapping
`compress_ratios` makes DSpark draft layers pick up target-layer
compress ratios and mix KV page sizes in the planner).

Running full-layer also matches the upstream four-card DeepSeek-V4 e2e
convention (no layer reduction outside dedicated trimming tests).

unmodified main source, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` local checkpoint):
**1 passed in 405s** — weights load (39.8 GiB/rank), KV planning

[BugFix][SpecDecode] Preserve tensor state when skipping drafts (#17274)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up to #16512. When drafting is skipped, the current code stores a
Python list of empty drafts. Async scheduling can already have reserved
speculative placeholders for the next step. The inherited
GPUModelRunner._prepare_input_ids requires a Tensor to scatter those
slots and asserts on the list.

- Pass SchedulerOutput into _skip_drafting.
- Publish an int32 zero Tensor on the runner device with shape
(num_reqs, configured num_spec_tokens).
- Call the existing _copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu(..., zeros_only=True),
refreshing the actual draft stride before its async early return and
publishing CPU zeros/request IDs/events only when needed.
- Preserve sampled-token/count updates and DP dummy behavior; clear
stale draft probabilities as before.

The full configured width covers all reserved slots, including reduced
per-step speculative widths. The zeros are draft candidates/placeholders
for normal target verification, not directly emitted output tokens. This
follows the representation already used on the 0.26 branch.

Add regression coverage for skip -> next async input preparation with
reordered requests and 1/3/5 speculative slots; verify sampled tokens
and zeros reach the correct positions. Exercise real CPU publication
logic for sync, structured output, penalties, and PP, including event
recording and untouched unused buffer rows. Check that stale previous
draft width is refreshed even when CPU publication is skipped.

Scope: no max-model-length threshold change, no removal of assertions,
and no unrelated n-gram state-handling change. The reported 131072 input
+ 1024 output with max_model_len=133120 does not by itself prove that
overflow occurred. Runtime SHA, actual metadata length and effective
drafter limit are still needed to attribute that incident.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Prevents a next-step Tensor assertion after the drafter-length skip
path. Normal drafting and configuration remain unchanged. No accuracy or
performance improvement is claimed without NPU evaluation.

### How was this patch tested?

AI assistance was used to implement and inspect these changes. The
submitter must review the changes and test intent before requesting
review.

[BugFix][Worker] Select local communication endpoints by bound NPU (#16249)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The NPU visible-to-physical device mapping from #16256 is merged in
upstream main as `9750add07ee64aa966ce2d03e86c8e070b46e9f6`. This PR
builds on that merged implementation and contains only the
endpoint-selection fix.

DP workers can share `local_rank=0` while binding different visible
NPUs. The old `setup_ascend_local_comm_res()` indexed
`ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` with this rank, which could select the wrong
`ub_endpoint_npu_<id>.json`. Containers exposing only part of a host's
NPUs additionally require runtime-to-host conversion.

Pass the bound `visible_device_index` from the worker into the helper,
then resolve its host physical ID through
`current_platform.visible_device_id_to_physical_device_id()` merged by
#16256. Select the endpoint file using that physical ID and propagate
mapping errors. Calls without endpoint configuration still return
without performing conversion.

Rebased onto upstream main `e2f7e3110` after #16256 merged. The PR now
contains one endpoint-fix commit and four files: `vllm_ascend/utils.py`,
`vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py`, `tests/ut/test_local_comm_res.py`, and
`tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py`. No prerequisite platform or
native-binding commits remain in this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Endpoint files configured through `ascend_local_comm_res_path` are
selected by the bound NPU's host physical ID. This uses the native
conversion binding already merged by #16256 and requires an extension
built with a supporting CANN version.

rank 0 and checked device count, host physical ID, real endpoint-file

[BugFix][Worker] Align MRV2 dummy LM-head TP before EPLB (#17233)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17232.

When a decode DP rank is idle, the MRV2 dummy path currently enters the
parent `_dummy_run()` EPLB step before it joins the LM-head TP
collective. An active rank samples through LM-head TP first and advances
EPLB afterward. In the QWEN3_235B_PD nightly configuration, this
opposite collective order produces an HCCL timeout.

Keep the existing dummy `compute_logits()` call after the parent's dummy
forward and speculator. Pass `skip_eplb=True` to the parent's decorated
`_dummy_run()`, then apply the same upstream
`step_eplb_after(is_dummy=True)` decorator to the Ascend override. The
resulting order is forward, dummy LM-head, EPLB, without unwrapping or
changing upstream methods. Preserve `skip_eplb`, profiling,
non-last-stage, and fixed logits capacity behavior. Add regression tests
for the collective order and skip paths.

The observed reproduction, including the pinned YAML and required PD,
DP, EP, EPLB, and LM-head TP settings, is in #17232. This change
overlaps the target-side dummy LM-head ordering part of #15079; that PR
also covers speculative draft alignment.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The affected MRV2 PD deployment can complete requests without this
collective-order timeout.

### How was this patch tested?

[Feature][KVPP] Reuse MTP cache exclusion for DSpark (#17119)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds fixed-length DSpark support to KVPP by reusing the existing MTP
draft-cache exclusion logic:

- Identify both MTP and DSpark draft caches from the
proposer/speculator's actual loader-discovered layer names, without
assuming contiguous indices, an offset after target layers, or a
model-specific depth field. The worker records ownership on its cache
modules for budgeting, allocation and runtime prefetch to consume
consistently.
- Keep draft cache bundles separate even when their numeric indices
overlap target indices or their names have no numeric index. Reject
missing draft ownership on a draft-bearing stage and cross-model
target-KV sharing; non-draft PP stages use an empty draft set.
- Keep draft caches independently allocated on each rank and included in
the memory budget, while excluding them from KVPP target-layer
partitioning and broadcasts.
- For sliding-window DSpark drafts, reuse upstream cache-spec conversion
before the worker returns its cache specifications. KVPP budgeting and
subsequent cache grouping use the same full-allocation specifications,
while attention computation remains sliding-window based.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Supports combining KVPP with fixed-length DSpark in eager mode. Existing
MTP behavior remains unchanged.

DSpark adaptive verification and dynamic speculative lengths are not
supported. Sliding-window drafts use full-sequence cache allocation
rather than reclaiming cache blocks outside the window to save memory.

### How was this patch tested?

Validated commit `87541d9b5`:

- **Ascend A3, Model Runner V1**: GLM-5.2-W4A8 + DSpark, TP8, with EP
and asynchronous scheduling enabled.
- Covered basic answers, chunked prefill, prefix caching, mixed
requests, and decoding across a cache block boundary. With KVPP off and
on, **all 548 output token IDs across 9 requests in 5 test cases matched
exactly**, including cached-token counts and finish reasons.
- All 8 workers confirmed that budget specifications matched actual
allocation specifications. KVPP managed all 78 target layers and
excluded all 3 draft layers.
- **61 unit tests passed** in the actual Ascend dependency environment;
**63 tests and 7 subtests passed** in the local isolated regression
harness. Unit coverage includes V1/V2 loader metadata, both MTP/DSpark
methods, non-contiguous/overlapping/non-numeric draft names, PP-local
ownership, missing metadata and explicit cross-model shared-cache
rejection.
- Ruff lint, formatting and diff checks passed.

[BugFix][Spec Decode] Restore DSpARK weight post-processing on MRV1 (#17258)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

#16347 moved Qwen3 DSpARK rotation alignment from `load_weights()` into
`post_process()`, but only MRV2 invokes the new hook. MRV1 consequently
loads the draft without aligning its projection with a rotated target.

Call the optional DSpARK `post_process()` hook with the target
configuration after embedding/lm_head sharing and before draft
hidden-state precomputation. This preserves the final aligned weights
and ensures precomputed hidden states use the updated projection.

The GLM-5.2 W4A8 DSpARK nightly on main `baa023ada` reported
first-position acceptance of 8.46% against an 84.55% minimum while GSM8K
accuracy remained 96.44%:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35631828275/job/106484161637.
The missing MRV1 hook is confirmed in that revision; acceptance recovery
still needs the nightly rerun.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Restores DSpARK draft post-processing on MRV1. No new configuration
options.
